body:
Closes #290

When the chosen Solve For optimizes into a same-axis position keep-out wall (jump up, wait behind a block, then continue), the closed-form dual recovery degenerates for that direction. Since #273 the jump still lands, but the deterministic seed can end up optimized the wrong way: e.g. `solve/j003` X/MIN reached only -27 of a -31.3 optimum, `taser-80t` X/MIN landed at +0.13 (wrong side of zero) instead of -0.30. This makes that direction reliable.

## The fix: level-set objective ascent

Feasibility does not depend on the Solve For direction, only the *optimization* into it does (a local SLP ascent that degenerates direction-dependently). So instead of a local ascent, rewrite the objective as a movable goal wall and bisect its level between the feasible witness's value and the weak-duality bound (`ClosedFormSolve.dualBound`); each rung is a **feasibility** solve (`SlpSolve` phase 1) seeded from the best point so far. Feasibility is the robust, direction-independent operation, so this reaches the direction's optimum where a local ascent stalls.

- New `LevelSetAscent.improve(...)`: monotone (never returns a worse objective than the witness), returns `null` when the ladder does not apply (a delta-facing/`Mode.F` wall leaves the dual bound undefined).
- Wired into `dualChain`'s non-closed-form returns (single jump: SLP, relaxation, reseeded SLP) and `LongRunSolver.hugObjective` (the multi-jump last window). The closed-form fast path is untouched, so the cost is paid only on the degenerate directions that need it. Chain label gains `-> level set` when it improves.
- Measured across the capture corpus, the ladder beats the plain SLP hug on 72 (capture, direction) pairs, frequently reaching ~100% of the remaining gap to the dual bound and correcting genuine wrong-direction results.

## dF constraints: informed, not fixed

A delta-facing (dF) constraint compiles to a facing wall (`Mode.F`), which the position-linear dual cannot represent, so the dual bound is undefined and the ladder is skipped. dF constraints are rare (ordinary keep-out walls are position constraints and are **not** affected). When one is present the solve still lands via the general search; the result panel shows an info notice (`AngleSolverEngine.DF_DIRECTION_NOTICE`) explaining the chosen direction is not deterministically optimized there. The notice persists through saves (`SaveFile.Result.notice`, absent in old files, ignored by old versions).

## Tests

- `LevelSetAscentTest` (slow): on j003 X/MIN, j012 Z/MAX, j008-bfneo Z/MIN, taser-80t X/MIN the ladder strictly beats the plain SLP hug by a conservative floor and stays feasible and within the dual bound.
- `DfDirectionGateTest` (fast): position-wall specs have no facing wall so the ladder runs; a dF constraint makes `LevelSetAscent.improve` return null (the gate the info notice is shown for).
- `DirectionNoticeSaveTest` (fast): the notice round-trips through a save; legacy results load with no notice.
- `:core:test` and `:core:test -PslowTests` green.

In-game QA pending (core-only change, one loader suffices).
title: feat: level-set objective ascent for degenerate solve directions
